sweptAxes.result: NEW LEADER. $4077.96 on 148 trades at 13.54% DD -- level with buy-and-hold BTC ($4105.94) at roughly a quarter of its 52.06% drawdown.

Built the last idea from the literature search: rank the universe by trailing Sharpe and trade only the leaders. It does NOT help returns. Tighter selection monotonically lowers the balance and lowers the drawdown, the same risk/return dial every other filter turned out to be: topN 12 gives $3685.85 at 10.96% DD, topN 3 gives $2363.77 at 7.81%. The nominal new best, topN 20 of 29 pairs at $4175.64, filters almost nothing -- it drops 5 trades of 148 for +2.4%, which is noise at this sample size, not selection working.

leader.honestNote: Above BTC buy-and-hold ($4105.94) for the first time, but the margin over the previous leader ($4077.96) comes from dropping 5 trades with a near-no-op filter setting. Treat $4078 and $4176 as the same number. The defensible claim is BTC's return at a quarter of BTC's drawdown, not beating it.

readThisFirst: breakout + a 200-day MA trend gate is the first config to beat its own random-entry null by a detectable margin (p=0.005, excess 1.55R vs an MDE of 1.34R), and it does it at a 12.43% drawdown against BTC's 52.06%. It is still the best of 1152 in-sample configurations, so treat it as the thing to attack next, not as a finding. Everything before it -- long tpR, long maxHold -- was buying exposure in a rising market.
unsweptAxes: new filters not yet in backtest.js
nextUp: A multi-timeframe series, so alignMode and the higher-TF bias are testable at all -- they are structurally dead in every single-TF run done so far, which means an entire dimension of the strategy has never been exercised. Then volatility-targeted position sizing, the remaining literature idea, and the only one that changes the balance without changing which trades are taken.

randomEntryNull.reading: The leader's entry rule is worth 0.0973R against a coin flip with identical geometry, and a random-entry account ends ABOVE it. No config's excess reaches what this test could detect, so the honest statement is not 'no edge' but 'no edge large enough to see through the noise a 100R target creates'.

breakout + ma200 gate (the leader).reading: The first configuration in this campaign whose excess over a matched-geometry random entry exceeds what the test can detect. It survives the harder version too: restricting the random entries to bars the 200-MA gate allows makes the excess LARGER, so the gate is not doing the work on its own. Caveat that has to stay attached: this is the best of ~1152 configurations searched on the same data, and at that many draws roughly 6 configs reach p<0.005 by chance. p=0.005 is not a discovery here, it is a reason to keep testing this one.

leveredLeader.reading: Not a better strategy, the same one levered 20x. A 94% drawdown means $1000 was worth about $60 at the low. Reported because the owner asked for the highest number; the drawdown is reported with it because the number is meaningless without it.

concentration.reading: Same shape as the earlier config, better on every margin. Positive in all three full years standalone. Survives losing any single pair (worst $2808 without ZEC, up from $2303). Survives restriction to the 16 full-history pairs at $2712, up from $2226. Still right-tailed: top 5 of 143 trades are 79.7% of all R, median trade -1.11R, win rate 39.2%, and dropping the ten best turns the mean negative. That is what trend following is; it is recorded so the mean is never read as a stable statistic. 143 trades fall on 98 distinct days, so the effective sample is smaller than the nominal one by 1.46x.
